items.prompt: An on-premises application needs low-latency local access to cloud-backed files while the authoritative data is stored in Amazon S3. Which Storage Gateway mode fits?
constraints: The application uses file shares.
Local access latency matters.
S3 is the cloud repository.

options.text: Evaluate a S3 File Gateway file share with a local cache, validating SMB or NFS compatibility, cache capacity, network bandwidth, and S3 object behavior.
Use a Volume Gateway because a file application always requires iSCSI block semantics.
Use Tape Gateway because all S3-backed data is accessed through virtual tapes.
Use Direct Connect alone because connectivity provides a file namespace.

feedback.Reason: S3 File Gateway exposes file shares with a local cache while storing objects in S3.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: File Gateway presents SMB or NFS shares and uses a local cache for frequently accessed data.
Details.scenarioApplication: The owner sizes the cache and uplink, sets share permissions, and defines how files become S3 objects and are protected.
Details.errorCorrection: Volume Gateway exposes block protocols, Tape Gateway serves backup software, and connectivity alone does not create a file service.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Cached file access depends on gateway health, cache space, bandwidth, and cloud synchronization.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Volume Gateway is an iSCSI block pattern, not a transparent file-share choice.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Tape Gateway is optimized for virtual tape workflows.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: A network link carries traffic but does not provide file semantics.

items.prompt: A File Gateway workload reads the same files repeatedly but has limited on-premises disk. What capacity question is most important?
constraints: The local cache is smaller than the working set.
The WAN link has finite bandwidth.
Read locality can be measured.

options.text: Size the cache from the active working set and outage or reconnect behavior, then monitor cache hit rate, evictions, and upload or download bandwidth.
Make the cache one byte because S3 provides local latency.
Delete cached data whenever the gateway is busy without considering write state.
Assume cache size controls S3 object durability.

feedback.Reason: The local cache absorbs frequently accessed data and affects latency and WAN dependence.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: File Gateway caches recently read or written data locally while synchronizing with S3.
Details.scenarioApplication: The architect measures locality, reserves safe cache space, alarms on pressure, and plans behavior during cloud or link disruption.
Details.errorCorrection: S3 does not make remote reads local, uncontrolled deletion can lose pending writes, and cache size does not define S3 durability.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A larger cache costs local storage but can reduce WAN latency and transfer dependence.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Remote object access still depends on the network and gateway.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Cache eviction must respect dirty or pending data and application correctness.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: S3 durability is a service property independent of local cache size.

items.prompt: An existing NAS application can use either SMB or NFS, but its identity and locking behavior must remain unchanged. What should be tested for a File Gateway migration?
constraints: The protocol is part of the application contract.
The application uses permissions and locking.
The cloud target is S3.

options.text: Test the selected SMB or NFS share, identity mapping, permissions, file naming, locking, metadata, and object conversion behavior with representative clients.
Assume SMB and NFS are interchangeable because both are file protocols.
Change to object APIs without reviewing the application.
Disable permissions to avoid protocol differences.

feedback.Reason: Hybrid file migration depends on protocol and semantic compatibility, not just reachability.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: File Gateway supports file protocols but maps file operations and metadata to S3 objects with service-specific behavior.
Details.scenarioApplication: The owner validates application reads and writes, identities, locking, and recovery before cutover.
Details.errorCorrection: SMB and NFS differ, object APIs require code changes, and disabling permissions is unsafe.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Gateway compatibility can accelerate migration but does not eliminate application-level semantic testing.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Protocol and identity semantics are materially different.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: An object API migration changes the application contract.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Removing controls creates a security and correctness failure.

items.prompt: An on-premises database needs iSCSI block volumes with most data in AWS but a frequently accessed working set local. Which Volume Gateway model should be evaluated?
constraints: The application requires block storage.
Local cache is available.
AWS is the durable volume backend.

options.text: Evaluate cached volumes, sizing the local cache and write buffer and validating latency, bandwidth, reconnect, and recovery behavior.
Use stored volumes because all data must be local when only a working set is local.
Use File Gateway because iSCSI is a file protocol.
Use Tape Gateway and present a virtual tape as a database block device.

feedback.Reason: Cached Volume Gateway keeps a working set local while storing the full volume in AWS.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Cached volumes use local cache and write buffer with the cloud volume as the primary storage location.
Details.scenarioApplication: The architect models cache locality, WAN capacity, write durability, and database recovery before deployment.
Details.errorCorrection: Stored volumes keep primary data on premises, File Gateway is file-level, and tape is not a block device.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Cached mode depends strongly on link and local cache behavior during outages or cache misses.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Stored mode is for primary local data with asynchronous cloud snapshots.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: iSCSI is a block protocol, not a file protocol.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Virtual tape does not expose a database block volume.

items.prompt: An on-premises application requires its primary block data to remain local, while cloud snapshots provide disaster recovery. Which Volume Gateway model is the fit?
constraints: Primary access must remain local.
Cloud copies are for backup or recovery.
The application uses iSCSI.

options.text: Evaluate stored volumes, keeping primary data on local disks and creating asynchronous cloud snapshots with an explicit restore runbook.
Use cached volumes and delete the local copy after the first upload.
Use File Gateway because snapshots automatically create iSCSI targets.
Use S3 Glacier as a live local block device.

feedback.Reason: Stored volumes keep primary volume data on premises and support cloud snapshots for protection.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Volume Gateway stored volumes write data locally and asynchronously back up point-in-time snapshots to S3.
Details.scenarioApplication: The owner sizes local disks, schedules snapshots, tests restoration, and documents the data-loss window.
Details.errorCorrection: Cached mode makes cloud storage primary, File Gateway exposes shares, and Glacier is not a block device.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Local primary access needs local capacity and gateway health; cloud snapshots are not zero-RPO replication.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Cached volumes use cloud primary storage and do not match the local-primary requirement.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: File Gateway does not create iSCSI targets.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Archive object storage is not a live block protocol.

items.prompt: A Volume Gateway continues receiving writes while the cloud link is temporarily degraded. Which local component needs capacity and monitoring?
constraints: The gateway accepts local writes.
The uplink can be interrupted.
Data must not be silently discarded.

options.text: Size and monitor the write buffer for the chosen gateway mode, alarm before exhaustion, and define behavior when the buffer cannot accept more writes.
Use the read cache as an unlimited write buffer without checking its state.
Disable cloud uploads so the gateway never experiences backpressure.
Delete old buffer blocks without checking whether they are dirty.

feedback.Reason: The write buffer absorbs local writes before data is uploaded and is a finite operational dependency.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Storage Gateway maintains local cache and write buffer areas with different roles and capacity needs.
Details.scenarioApplication: The owner reserves capacity, alarms on pressure and upload lag, and plans application throttling or recovery for prolonged link loss.
Details.errorCorrection: Read cache is not an unlimited dirty-write store, disabling uploads loses protection, and deleting dirty blocks risks data loss.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: More local buffer capacity improves outage tolerance but does not create unlimited durability or bandwidth.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Cache and write buffer have separate purposes and finite capacity.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Stopping uploads increases backlog and recovery risk.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Dirty data must not be removed without a valid protection and application decision.

items.prompt: A backup application writes virtual tapes and expects a tape library interface while backups are retained in AWS. Which Storage Gateway type is appropriate?
constraints: The backup software is tape-oriented.
The target is cloud-backed archival storage.
The application should avoid a backup software rewrite.

options.text: Evaluate Tape Gateway, validating virtual tape library compatibility, cache and upload behavior, retention, retrieval time, and backup catalog recovery.
Use File Gateway because backup software can always write tape images as ordinary files.
Use cached volumes because virtual tapes are block volumes.
Use Direct Connect as the tape library interface.

feedback.Reason: Tape Gateway presents a virtual tape library for existing tape-aware backup applications.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Tape Gateway provides virtual tapes and a virtual tape library backed by AWS storage and archive workflows.
Details.scenarioApplication: The owner tests backup, catalog, virtual tape retrieval, archive transition, and recovery of the backup system itself.
Details.errorCorrection: File shares and block volumes are different backup targets, and network connectivity does not present a tape library.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Archive retrieval time and catalog integrity affect RTO and must be included in the design.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: A file share changes the target protocol and may require backup software changes.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: A volume gateway is not a virtual tape library.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Direct Connect carries traffic but does not emulate backup hardware.

items.prompt: A File Gateway has adequate cache but misses its upload target during the nightly data window. What is the first performance review?
constraints: The data volume is known.
The WAN link is shared.
Upload time is an operational objective.

options.text: Measure changed bytes, object conversion overhead, gateway CPU and disk, available uplink bandwidth, packet loss, and competing traffic before changing the cache.
Increase cache size and assume upload throughput will double.
Move the gateway cache to S3 because local disk is the bottleneck by definition.
Reduce the backup retention policy without checking transfer volume or compliance.

feedback.Reason: Upload performance is an end-to-end gateway, disk, network, and workload problem.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Gateway upload rate is bounded by changed-data volume, local resources, network path, and cloud processing.
Details.scenarioApplication: The owner correlates gateway metrics with link utilization and schedules or shapes traffic based on measured bottlenecks.
Details.errorCorrection: Cache size helps locality and outage tolerance but does not create WAN bandwidth, and retention changes need approval.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: More bandwidth or scheduling can improve the window but has network and transfer cost.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Cache size and uplink throughput are separate constraints.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: The gateway requires local cache and write-buffer resources.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Retention changes data protection and compliance, not just performance.

items.prompt: A business-critical hybrid application cannot depend on one virtual gateway host. What availability design should be assessed?
constraints: The application has a gateway dependency.
A local infrastructure failure is possible.
The service supports a controlled failover design.

options.text: Evaluate a supported gateway high-availability deployment, shared or replicated local infrastructure as applicable, and a tested failover and cache-recovery procedure.
Run two unrelated gateways against the same local cache disks without a supported coordination model.
Use a second gateway in another Region and assume local clients fail over without DNS or routing changes.
Rely on a larger cache instead of gateway redundancy.

feedback.Reason: Gateway redundancy must use a supported deployment and include local state, routing, and recovery behavior.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Storage Gateway availability depends on the virtual appliance or hardware host, local disks, network, and supported HA mechanisms.
Details.scenarioApplication: The owner tests host, network, and cloud failures and records how clients reconnect and how cached or buffered data is protected.
Details.errorCorrection: Uncoordinated shared disks can corrupt state, remote gateways need explicit routing, and cache size is not redundancy.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: HA can reduce local failure impact but adds infrastructure, testing, and operational complexity.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Stateful appliances need a supported coordination and storage design.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Cross-Region placement does not automatically change local client routing or namespace.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: A larger cache only increases outage tolerance; it does not remove a host failure.

items.prompt: An on-premises link to AWS fails while a File Gateway serves a hot working set. What should the application owner know?
constraints: The cache contains only part of the namespace.
The link may be unavailable for hours.
Writes and reads have different behavior.

options.text: Document which cached reads and writes can continue, what happens on cache miss or dirty-buffer pressure, and how applications enter an explicit degraded or paused state.
Assume all files remain available because the gateway has a local cache.
Delete the gateway cache so every request fails visibly.
Treat the gateway as an independent durable copy of every S3 object.

feedback.Reason: A gateway cache is finite and does not make the entire cloud namespace locally available during link loss.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Cache hits may remain local, while misses, uploads, and dirty data depend on the gateway and cloud path.
Details.scenarioApplication: The runbook names safe operations, alarms on backlog, and directs the application to a visible degraded mode rather than silent data loss.
Details.errorCorrection: Not every file is cached, deleting cache can destroy useful state, and cache is not an independent full durable copy.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Larger local resources extend some outage behavior but do not remove the network dependency.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Only cached data has local access behavior; cache misses depend on the link.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Destructive cache removal is not an outage strategy.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: The cache is not automatically a complete independent backup.

items.prompt: A gateway deployment allocates local disks without distinguishing cache from write buffer. Why is that a design error?
constraints: The gateway handles reads and writes.
The disks have different performance and durability characteristics.
An outage can create backlog.

options.text: Assign and size local disks by gateway role, separating read cache and write buffer capacity, performance, monitoring, and failure handling.
Use any disk for any role because Storage Gateway treats all local disks identically.
Allocate only write buffer disks for a read-heavy File Gateway.
Use S3 as the local disk for gateway cache pages.

feedback.Reason: Local gateway disk roles have different effects on read locality and pending writes.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Storage Gateway uses local cache and upload buffer areas with separate capacity and performance implications.
Details.scenarioApplication: The architect labels disks, reserves headroom, monitors each role, and rehearses disk loss and replacement procedures.
Details.errorCorrection: Disks are not interchangeable in their operational role, write-only allocation misses read demand, and S3 is remote object storage.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Faster or redundant local disks can improve gateway behavior but increase infrastructure cost.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Role assignment affects gateway behavior and recovery.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: A read-heavy workload still needs cache capacity.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Remote S3 cannot serve as local gateway disk space.

items.prompt: A branch office shares a constrained WAN link with business traffic and nightly file uploads. What operational design reduces contention?
constraints: The link is finite.
Transfer demand is predictable.
Business traffic needs priority.

options.text: Measure the transfer window, shape or schedule gateway traffic where supported, reserve network headroom, and alarm on upload backlog and application latency.
Allow storage traffic to consume the entire link because uploads are more important than users.
Disable caching so all file access uses the link equally.
Increase S3 storage capacity to create WAN bandwidth.

feedback.Reason: Hybrid performance is constrained by shared WAN capacity and needs explicit traffic management.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Gateway synchronization and client access share the network path with other branch traffic.
Details.scenarioApplication: The owner establishes QoS or scheduling, tracks changed bytes and backlog, and validates that user SLOs remain protected.
Details.errorCorrection: Unbounded storage traffic harms users, disabling cache increases network dependence, and S3 capacity does not change WAN bandwidth.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Scheduling can lengthen upload completion and must be checked against protection objectives.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Unbounded transfer traffic creates a predictable contention failure.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Disabling cache increases WAN reads and does not solve contention.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Storage capacity is independent of network capacity.

items.prompt: A File Gateway share should be reachable only by approved on-premises subnets and should encrypt cloud traffic. Which controls are relevant?
constraints: The gateway has a private or controlled network path.
Share-level and cloud permissions differ.
Data protection requirements are explicit.

options.text: Use network segmentation and firewall or security controls for clients, share permissions and identity controls, and encrypted gateway communication with least-privilege AWS access.
Rely on the S3 bucket name as the only access control for on-premises clients.
Expose the gateway management interface to the public internet for convenience.
Disable encryption because local clients already use a private VLAN.

feedback.Reason: Hybrid storage has separate local network, share, and cloud authorization boundaries.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Clients reach gateway protocols locally while the gateway calls AWS services using credentials, policies, and encrypted transport.
Details.scenarioApplication: The owner limits client subnets, protects management access, constrains S3 actions, and verifies encryption and audit logging.
Details.errorCorrection: Bucket naming is not local authorization, public management exposure is unsafe, and a private VLAN does not remove cloud encryption needs.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Private connectivity and least privilege require network and IAM operations that must be maintained during changes.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: S3 policy does not define which local hosts can connect to a share.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Management-plane exposure increases attack surface.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Local network privacy does not replace encryption in transit to AWS.

items.prompt: A stored Volume Gateway workload needs disaster recovery in AWS after a local appliance loss. What must the runbook use?
constraints: Cloud snapshots exist.
The replacement environment is in a VPC.
The application recovery objective is defined.

options.text: Restore a volume from a validated gateway snapshot or supported cloud copy, attach it to the recovery path, and validate filesystem and application consistency before cutover.
Assume the local gateway cache is a complete backup after appliance loss.
Create an empty volume with the same label and start the application.
Use a File Gateway share as a transparent replacement for the block volume.

feedback.Reason: Gateway snapshots provide a recovery source, but restoration and application validation remain customer responsibilities.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Volume Gateway snapshots create cloud copies that can support a replacement volume or recovery design.
Details.scenarioApplication: The owner restores in a controlled environment, checks filesystem and application state, and records the snapshot time as part of RPO.
Details.errorCorrection: Cache is not a guaranteed complete backup, labels do not restore data, and file shares do not replace block semantics.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Snapshot recovery has restore time, transfer, and possible data-loss windows that must fit the RTO and RPO.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Local cache state can be incomplete or unavailable with the appliance.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: A new empty volume has no application data.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: File and block protocols are not transparent substitutes.

items.prompt: A gateway appliance needs software updates without losing service or creating an unobserved outage. Which procedure is appropriate?
constraints: The gateway is production.
The client application has a maintenance tolerance.
The team can test failover or pause behavior.

options.text: Review supported maintenance behavior, protect and monitor local state, schedule a controlled window or failover, and validate clients and synchronization afterward.
Apply updates to every gateway simultaneously without checking state.
Delete the gateway and recreate it because managed services never retain configuration.
Stop monitoring during maintenance to avoid false alarms.

feedback.Reason: A gateway is a stateful hybrid dependency and maintenance needs a controlled operational procedure.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Gateway software, local cache or buffer state, client mounts, and cloud synchronization all affect maintenance risk.
Details.scenarioApplication: The owner uses supported update procedures, verifies health and backlog before and after, and keeps an explicit client recovery path.
Details.errorCorrection: Fleet-wide changes increase blast radius, recreation can lose state, and monitoring is required during changes.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Maintenance windows and redundancy reduce risk but add operational planning and test work.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Uncontrolled simultaneous updates remove a safe recovery path.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Recreation is not a generic maintenance procedure for stateful gateways.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Monitoring is essential to detect failed updates and backlog.

items.prompt: Which observations best show that a Storage Gateway is approaching a performance or availability boundary?
constraints: The gateway serves production clients.
The cloud link can saturate.
The team needs leading indicators.

options.text: Correlate cache and buffer utilization, upload or download backlog, gateway health, disk and network metrics, client latency, and cloud service errors.
Monitor only total S3 capacity.
Alarm only after an application write fails.
Use the number of files as the sole gateway performance metric.

feedback.Reason: Gateway limits span local resources, synchronization, network, and client behavior.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: CloudWatch gateway metrics expose cache, buffer, health, and transfer conditions that can precede application failures.
Details.scenarioApplication: Operators establish thresholds and correlate metrics with workload windows to throttle, add resources, or invoke recovery before SLO breach.
Details.errorCorrection: S3 capacity is not gateway health, write-failure alarms are late, and file count is only an indirect workload signal.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: More monitoring needs threshold tuning and retention but makes hybrid degradation visible.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: S3 capacity does not show local cache pressure or link backlog.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Failure-only detection leaves no response margin.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: File count does not describe bytes, locality, operations, or network rate.

items.prompt: An application writes files through File Gateway and another process reads the corresponding S3 objects directly. What consistency boundary must be documented?
constraints: Both file and object interfaces are used.
The application has ordering expectations.
The gateway uploads changed data asynchronously.

options.text: Define when file writes are uploaded and visible as S3 objects, avoid assuming a synchronous dual interface, and test the application workflow and retry behavior.
Assume a successful local file write means every S3 reader immediately sees the final object.
Use S3 versioning as a substitute for defining upload completion.
Delete the local file immediately after the write to force synchronization.

feedback.Reason: File Gateway bridges file and object interfaces but has synchronization behavior that must be treated as an explicit boundary.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Gateway uploads file changes to S3 and maps file operations to objects; local success and object visibility are distinct events.
Details.scenarioApplication: The owner uses a completion signal or workflow boundary, tests retries and overwrites, and documents which interface is authoritative.
Details.errorCorrection: Local write success does not prove cloud upload completion, versioning preserves history but not workflow timing, and deletion can lose data.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Using one interface as the system of record simplifies semantics but can limit integration patterns.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Upload is a separate synchronization step.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Versioning helps recovery but does not define when a change is available.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Local deletion before upload completion is unsafe.

items.prompt: A company creates separate File Gateway shares for teams and needs to prevent namespace and access overlap in S3. What configuration decision matters?
constraints: The shares have different owners.
Cloud object access is also controlled.
The S3 namespace must be predictable.

options.text: Map shares to deliberately scoped S3 buckets or prefixes, align gateway share permissions with bucket policies, and test object ownership and naming behavior.
Use one unrestricted bucket because local share names enforce all cloud isolation.
Create one bucket per file without considering service limits or operational overhead.
Use IAM admin access for every share so mappings cannot fail.

feedback.Reason: File share isolation and S3 object isolation are separate configuration surfaces that must align.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: File Gateway shares map file namespaces to S3 locations, while IAM and bucket policies govern cloud access.
Details.scenarioApplication: The owner defines prefix or bucket ownership, least-privilege roles, object tags or metadata, and cross-interface tests.
Details.errorCorrection: Local names do not enforce cloud isolation, one bucket per file is operationally poor, and admin access violates least privilege.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Separate buckets simplify ownership but increase resource management; prefixes can scale but need policy precision.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Cloud readers can bypass local share names unless bucket policy scopes them.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Per-file buckets create avoidable service and operations complexity.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Administrative access hides mapping errors and broadens blast radius.

items.prompt: A File Gateway cache disk fails and the team can recreate the cache from S3. What recovery concern remains?
constraints: S3 is the authoritative repository.
The gateway has a replacement cache disk.
The application has latency and consistency requirements.

options.text: Rebuild the cache through the supported procedure, verify pending writes and object integrity, and expect a warm-up period with changed read latency and WAN demand.
Assume cache replacement is invisible because S3 objects are already local.
Delete the S3 bucket before rebuilding to avoid stale data.
Use a snapshot of the cache disk as the only cloud copy.

feedback.Reason: A cache can be recreated, but locality, pending writes, and network load change during recovery.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: The gateway cache is a performance layer while S3 remains the cloud repository; cache loss can cause misses and rehydration traffic.
Details.scenarioApplication: The owner confirms the last synchronized state, monitors rebuild and bandwidth, and communicates a degraded performance window.
Details.errorCorrection: S3 objects are remote to the gateway, deleting the bucket is destructive, and a cache snapshot is not necessarily the complete source.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Rebuilding from the cloud reduces durable-data loss risk but can increase latency and transfer cost during warm-up.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Remote S3 data still needs to be fetched into the cache.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Destructive deletion removes the recovery source.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: The cache is a local performance layer and may not represent all data or state.

items.prompt: A hybrid design claims a one-hour recovery objective but relies on weekly gateway snapshots and a slow link. What must be corrected?
constraints: The RTO and RPO are business requirements.
Snapshots and transfer have measurable intervals.
Recovery must be rehearsed.

options.text: Translate the RTO and RPO into snapshot frequency, transfer bandwidth, restore time, application validation, and cutover steps, then test the complete recovery path.
Keep weekly snapshots because a gateway automatically reduces recovery time.
Increase local cache size and assume it guarantees a cloud recovery point.
Use a faster file protocol without changing protection frequency or restore steps.

feedback.Reason: Recovery objectives must be backed by protection frequency, transfer, restore, and validation capabilities.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Gateway snapshots and data uploads create measurable RPO and restore dependencies; local cache is not the recovery plan.
Details.scenarioApplication: The owner models changed data, link time, snapshot cadence, restore duration, and application checks against the objective.
Details.errorCorrection: Managed gateway behavior does not erase snapshot age, cache does not guarantee cloud copy, and protocol choice alone does not fix recovery.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Meeting a tighter objective may require more bandwidth, frequent copies, standby resources, or a different architecture.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Weekly snapshots cannot meet a one-hour data-loss objective.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Local cache can be lost with the appliance and is not an independent recovery point.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Protocol latency does not establish a protection or restore schedule.

items.prompt: An enterprise wants predictable private connectivity from its data center to a Storage Gateway VPC endpoint. Which connectivity review is needed?
constraints: The gateway remains private.
The data center has hybrid routing.
The service endpoint and DNS must resolve correctly.

options.text: Evaluate Direct Connect, VPN, routing, endpoint access, DNS, MTU, redundancy, and bandwidth against the gateway's latency and availability requirements.
Use Direct Connect without redundant paths because the circuit is always available.
Assume a VPC endpoint automatically advertises routes to the data center.
Expose the gateway publicly to avoid all route configuration.

feedback.Reason: A hybrid gateway depends on the complete private network path, not merely the existence of a circuit or endpoint.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Private connectivity requires routing, DNS, endpoint policy, security controls, and resilient paths between clients and AWS.
Details.scenarioApplication: The architect tests both directions, failover, name resolution, packet size, and throughput with realistic gateway traffic.
Details.errorCorrection: A single circuit is a failure domain, endpoints do not automatically publish enterprise routes, and public exposure increases risk.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Redundant connectivity improves availability but costs more and requires operational coordination.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: The circuit itself can fail and needs a resilience plan.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Enterprise routing and DNS still need explicit configuration.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Public exposure is not a substitute for controlled private connectivity.

items.prompt: A review compares File Gateway, Volume Gateway, Tape Gateway, DataSync, and direct cloud storage for an on-premises workload. What decision criterion is primary?
constraints: The existing application contract is known.
Latency, protocol, protection, and migration scope matter.
The hybrid dependency must be supportable.

options.text: Start with the required protocol and access semantics, then evaluate cache or buffer behavior, bandwidth, consistency, recovery, identity, cost, and operational ownership.
Choose the service with the most storage capacity regardless of protocol.
Choose Storage Gateway for every migration because it always provides the lowest latency.
Choose direct S3 access even when the application requires iSCSI or SMB semantics.

feedback.Reason: Hybrid storage services solve different interface and migration problems and must be selected from the application contract.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: File, block, tape, transfer, and object services have distinct protocols, latency boundaries, consistency, and operational models.
Details.scenarioApplication: The architect chooses one canonical path that satisfies the workload and validates migration and recovery rather than layering incompatible interfaces.
Details.errorCorrection: Capacity does not establish protocol fit, Gateway is not always lowest latency, and S3 is not SMB or iSCSI.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A local gateway can preserve legacy access but introduces appliance, link, cache, and synchronization dependencies.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Capacity is not a substitute for application protocol compatibility.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Gateway adds local performance but has network and appliance dependencies.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Direct object access requires an application or adapter change when file or block semantics are required.
